defect.description: The setting is read as settings['FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE'] or False instead of settings.getbool(...): command-line overrides arrive as text, so -s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False (or =0) gives the non-empty string 'False', which is truthy and turns active mode on.

review_items: feedstorage.py:27 uses raw settings access with `or False` instead of getbool, so command-line 'False'/'0' strings are truthy and enable active mode
Tests only pass native bools; add from_command_line string-value tests
votes.evidence_quote: `settings["FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE"] or False` reads the raw value via `__getitem__` instead of using `getbool`; when the setting is set on the command line as `-s FEED_STORAGE_FTP_ACTIVE=False`, the value is the string `"False"`, and `"False" or False` evaluates to `"False"` (truthy), so active mode is enabled even though the user explicitly disabled it.
votes.justification: The review identifies the exact code in from_settings, the cause (raw string access instead of getbool), and the faulty behaviour: a command-line 'False' or '0' is truthy and enables active mode.
